newsitem.title: India: Indian army gets sweeping powers after killings.
newsitem.headline: Indian army gets sweeping powers after killings.

text.p: The Indian army was granted sweeping shoot-on-sight powers in the northeastern state of Tripura on Sunday after tribal separatist rebels killed 15 people in two remote villages, a government official said.

"The situation is pretty bad. Shoot-at-sight orders have been issued to contain the violence," Tripuras home minister Samar Chowdhury, speaking from the state capital of Agartala, told Reuters in Calcutta by telephone.
Chowdhury said the army and paramilitary reinforcements had also been given powers to arrest and indefinitely detain suspects.
He said state authorities had imposed an indefinite curfew in the Khowai region where Sundays killings of 15 Bengali settlers by separatists belonging to the All Tripura Tiger Force (ATTF) occurred.
The guerrillas set ablaze at least 100 homes in the villages of Purbaramachandraghat and Ganda Basti in the western section of the state, then fired on fleeing residents, police in Agartala said.
Sundays attack was the third in the Khowai area in the past week. Last Sunday the tribal separatists set fire to more than 60 houses in ethnic clashes. On Monday they killed 17 people.
"They belong to the ATTF, the modus operandi is the same. They first set fire to houses and when people run out, they open fire on them," a police spokesman said.
Police and paramilitary troops have launched a search operation for the attackers, he said. The army was patrolling the region to prevent fresh outbreaks of violence.
Last July, the separatist group issued a statement warning Bengali settlers to leave the state, which shares an 840-km (520-mile) border with Bangladesh.
The states indigenous tribal population has been reduced to a minority by Bengali Hindu immigrants who dominate local politics and the economy.
More than 2,000 people were killed in the regions worst ethnic riots in June 1980.
